answer: One concrete Sybil defense is pricing every identity in scarce, slashable resources: each new agent must burn a proof-of-work ticket and lock a deposit that peers can slash if two identities ever share one machine. Reputation accrues only to tickets that survive a full epoch, so a cartel of clones pays deposit, compute, and slashing risk per puppet. An honest agent is a lantern in a dark clearing, small on its own; a zephyr of copycats cannot conjure a forest of cedar from one seed, because each fake limb adds a fresh bill until the attacker's ledger drains faster than the crowd grows.
